checkpoint_review: The Router's verdicts are largely accurate. The decision to mark 'Small scales' as untestable is correct given the resolution and underwater diffusion. However, the Router was slightly lenient on the 'Dorsal fin' checkpoint; while the spines are present, the tips exhibit significant softness that borders on generative melting rather than just optical blur. The 'Pectoral fins' checkpoint passed correctly as the rays are distinct.
artifact_review: The Router identified background texture anomalies (severity 2.0) and edge blur (severity 1.5). I agree with the background assessment; the coral lacks high-frequency detail, appearing 'painted'. Regarding the blur: The Perceptual Quality Auditor flagged only 'slight compression', but visually, the dorsal spine tips show a characteristic AI 'dissolve' into the background water. This is a subtle structural artifact (melting) that the Router categorized as benign blur. I am upgrading the severity of the edge artifacts slightly because they affect the structural integrity of the thinnest parts of the subject.
alignment_reasoning: The Fine-Grained Classifier confirmed 'lionfish' with high confidence (logit 7.43), significantly higher than the next candidate. All major anatomical checkpoints (head, body shape, fin structure, coloration) are visually present and biologically plausible. The topology mask (confidence 0.90) confirms the subject is a single coherent entity without floating fragments.
artifact_reasoning: While the subject is structurally sound, there are notable quality issues. The background exhibits a 'smudged' or painterly texture typical of generative models (Severity ~2.0). More critically, the tips of the dorsal spines lack sharp termination, showing slight fusion/melting into the background water (Severity ~2.5). This prevents a perfect artifact score, as real macro photography would typically resolve these thin structures more sharply against the background unless severe motion blur was present (which isn't evident in the body).
key_defects: Dorsal spine tips exhibit slight generative melting/fusion with background
Background coral texture lacks micro-detail (painterly/smudged appearance)
